results.summary: This project implements a 2-bit adder using combinational logic, with inputs IN1 through IN4 and outputs OUT1 through OUT3. An additional inverter connects IN0 to OUT0, which is not part of the adder. Testing involves toggling the inputs and observing the outputs to verify the addition. External hardware such as an LED display is needed to view the results. The design is a simple educational example created in the Wokwi environment.

This design is a simple counter that increments a displayed number on a 7-segment display, with step and reset buttons for manual control. It uses basic logic gates to drive the display segments based on the counter's output. Optionally, a clock source can be connected for automatic counting. The project serves as an introductory exercise in digital logic and display interfacing within the Wokwi environment.

This project is a full adder circuit with three inputs (two 1-bit operands and a carry-in) and two outputs (sum and carry-out). The outputs are intended to drive two LEDs, one red and one blue, to indicate the sum and carry bits. Testing instructions are minimal, but the design can be verified by applying input combinations and observing the LED states. It is a basic educational schematic created in Wokwi.

This project implements an 8-bit reverse counter using a series of D flip-flops. It includes reset and step buttons for manual control, and the outputs are designed to drive LEDs. The counter operates at a 10 Hz clock when in automatic mode. It is a straightforward digital design created in Wokwi, suitable for learning about counters and sequential logic.

This design consists of two D flip-flops connected to the input and output pins. The D inputs are IN0 and IN2, and the corresponding Q outputs are OUT0 and OUT2. The documentation is minimal, providing only a basic description and test method. It appears to be a simple educational project created in Wokwi.

This project is a 4-bit adder with a carry output, implemented using XOR, AND, and OR gates based on a reference schematic. It takes two 4-bit inputs (A and B) and produces a 4-bit sum plus carry. Testing involves feeding input values and observing the outputs, which can be displayed using LEDs. External hardware such as switches and LEDs is required for input and output. The design is an educational exercise created in Wokwi.

This project is a simple guessing game where the user attempts to guess a number; if correct, an LED lights up. It has a single input (IN3) and a single output (OUT0) intended to drive an LED. The documentation is very sparse, providing only a brief description and test instruction. It appears to be a beginner's project created in Wokwi.

This design converts a 4-bit input into signals for a 7-segment display using combinational logic. It includes a decimal point output that is always on. Testing involves setting each input individually to verify the corresponding digit is displayed. The project is a straightforward educational exercise created in Wokwi, requiring an external 7-segment display for output.

This project implements a 3-bit full adder with inputs A (IN0-IN2), B (IN3-IN5), and carry-in (IN6), producing a 3-bit sum (OUT0-OUT2) and carry-out (OUT3). The documentation notes a discrepancy in the bit assignments, but the intended function is clear. Testing involves toggling switches and observing the output on hex 7-segment LEDs. It is an educational design created in Wokwi.

This project is a 4-bit ripple counter that also includes a NAND gate and an AND gate. It has a clock input (CLK) and four additional inputs (IN0-IN3), with six outputs (OUT0-OUT5). Testing instructions are minimal, suggesting the use of a DIP switch and hex LED for input and output. The design is an initial test of a Wokwi implementation, likely for educational purposes.
